t.7.34.1: Released by Arjuna, Rāvaṇa, the lord of the Rākṣasas, roamed over the whole earth, undaunted even though he had been treated in that way.
t.7.34.2: Whatever rākṣasa or man Rāvaṇa hears of as superior in strength, him the arrogant Rāvaṇa approaches and challenges to battle.
t.7.34.3: Then one day, having gone to the city of Kiṣkindhā, which was protected by Vālin, he challenged Vālin, who wore a golden garland, to battle.
t.7.34.4: Then Tāra, the minister of the vānaras, the mighty father of Tārā, spoke these words to Rāvaṇa, who had arrived eager for battle.
t.7.34.5: O lord of the Rākṣasas, Vālī, who could be a match for you, has gone away. No other monkey is able to stand before you.
t.7.34.6: Rāvaṇa, having performed the twilight worship at all four oceans, Vālin is returning this very moment; wait a little while.
t.7.34.7: Behold these heaps of bones, white as conch-shells; these, O King, are the remains of those who sought battle, slain by the might of the lord of the Vānaras.
t.7.34.8: Even if you have drunk the elixir of immortality, O Rāvaṇa, O rākṣasa, still, once you have encountered Vālin, that will be the end of your life.
t.7.34.9: Or, if you are in haste to die, go to the southern ocean; there you will see Vālin, like the sun standing upon the earth.
t.7.34.10: But Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, having sharply rebuked Tāra, mounted that Puṣpaka and set out for the southern ocean.
t.7.34.11: There Rāvaṇa saw Vālin, who resembled a golden mountain, whose face shone like the rising sun, and who was intent on performing his twilight worship.
t.7.34.12: Then Rāvaṇa, dark as collyrium, descended from the Puṣpaka and swiftly ran forward with noiseless steps to seize Vālin.
t.7.34.13: That Rāvaṇa, bent on wicked intent, was seen by Vālin, who happened to open his eyes, yet he showed no alarm.
t.7.34.14: As a lion on spotting a hare, or as Garuḍa on spotting a serpent, pays it no heed, so Vālī gave no thought to that Rāvaṇa, whose purpose was wicked.
t.7.34.15: Today I shall make this evil-minded Rāvaṇa, who seeks to seize me, dangle from my armpit, and so go to the great oceans.
t.7.34.16: They will see my enemy Daśagrīva clasped at my side, his thighs, arms and garments drooping limply, dangling like a serpent held by Garuḍa.
t.7.34.17: Having thus made up his mind, Vālī, keeping his ear alert, stood like the king of mountains, muttering the Vedic mantras.
t.7.34.18: Each eager to seize the other, the king of the monkeys and the king of the rākṣasas, proud of their strength, strove with great effort at that deed.
t.7.34.19: Judging by the sound of his footsteps that Rāvaṇa was now within reach of his hand, Vālī, though his face was turned away, seized him as a bird seizes a serpent.
t.7.34.20: Seizing that lord of the Rākṣasas, who had been eager to seize him, the monkey made him dangle from his armpit and with great speed leapt up into the sky.
t.7.34.21: Squeezing him tightly, Vālī carried off Rāvaṇa, who kept clawing at him again and again with his nails, as the wind carries off a rain-cloud.
t.7.34.22: Then, as Daśānana was being carried off, those fearsome rākṣasa ministers, eager to set him free, rushed forward, roaring loudly.
t.7.34.23: Followed by them, Vālī shone as he moved through the midst of the sky, like the sun stationed in the heavens followed by masses of clouds.
t.7.34.24: Those foremost of rākṣasas, unable to match Vālin who had come upon them, fall down utterly exhausted by the speed of his arms and thighs.
t.7.34.25: For the lords of the mountains moved aside from the path of Vālin as he went along.
t.7.34.26: The lord of the monkeys, of great speed, whose flight no flocks of birds could follow, performed the twilight worship at all the oceans one after another.
t.7.34.27: Honored by the sky-roaming beings, the sky-ranging monkey Vālin came to the western ocean with Rāvaṇa.
t.7.34.28: There the monkey bathed, performed the twilight worship and recited his prayers, and then, carrying Daśānana, he went on to the northern ocean.
t.7.34.29: Having performed the twilight worship at the northern sea, Vālī, still carrying the Ten-faced one, went to the eastern ocean, the great treasury of waters.
t.7.34.30: Having performed the evening twilight worship there as well, Vāsavi, that lord of the monkeys, seized Rāvaṇa and, facing toward Kiṣkindhā, came back again.
t.7.34.31: Having performed the twilight worship at all four oceans, the monkey, wearied from carrying Rāvaṇa, descended in a grove near Kiṣkindhā.
t.7.34.32: Then the best of monkeys released Rāvaṇa from his armpit, and, laughing, he said to Rāvaṇa, "Where have you come from?"
t.7.34.34: O lord of monkeys, radiant as great Indra, I am Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas. Eager for battle I have come, and today I have found you at last.
t.7.34.33: Having fallen into great astonishment, the lord of the Rākṣasas, gazing wearily about the world, spoke these words to that lord of the monkeys.
t.7.34.35: Ah, your strength! Ah, your valour! Ah, your profundity! For you seized me like a beast and whirled me around the four oceans.
t.7.34.36: O hero, O monkey, what other hero will stride like this, so swiftly and as if never tiring, while carrying even me?
t.7.34.37: O monkey, such speed belongs to three beings alone: the mind, the wind and Suparṇa, or else to you; of this there is no doubt.
t.7.34.38: Having witnessed your strength, O bull among monkeys, I desire with you a lasting and deeply affectionate friendship, sworn in the presence of the fire.
t.7.34.39: Wives, sons, city, kingdom, pleasures, clothing and food: all of this shall be shared between the two of us, undivided, O lord of the monkeys.
t.7.34.40: Then, having kindled a fire, the two of them, the monkey and the rākṣasa, embraced each other and entered into brotherhood.
t.7.34.41: Then those two, the monkey and the rākṣasa, holding each other by the hand, joyfully entered Kiṣkindhā, like two lions entering a mountain cave.
t.7.34.42: The base Rāvaṇa dwelt there for a month like Sugrīva, together with his ministers who had come, men eager to lay waste the three worlds.
t.7.34.43: Thus, O lord, did this happen of old: Rāvaṇa was overpowered by Vālin and was also made his brother in the presence of fire.
t.7.34.44: O Rāma, Vālin possessed supreme, matchless strength; yet even he was utterly consumed by you, as a moth is by fire.
